body.statement: Among all admissible positive even population sizes not exceeding eight, the equality set is exactly \(\{2,4,6\}\), and \(n=8\) is the first size at which compressing \((X_1,X_0)\) to \(W\) is minimax-lossy for ATE squared error.
body.justification: This is the finite threshold result that turns four isolated calculations into one interpretable theorem.
body.gap: The closest papers leave unrestricted complete-randomization behavior unresolved and do not identify a first sample-size cutoff for count compression.
body.consumer: DeclareDesign users receive the first exact sample size at which the conventional count difference ceases to be a minimax-preserving data reduction.
